newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard lawsuit alleges bad pricing on muni index.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard lawsuit alleges bad pricing on muni index.

text.p: Vanguard Municipal Bond Fund Inc has filed suit against Thomson Publishing Corp, a unit of Thomson Corp, and six muni brokers, alleging the fund lost at least $3.25 million as a result of incorrect pricing on the index backing the muni futures contract.

In the suit, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, Vanguard said it held 3,420 municipal futures contracts on December 19, 1995. It said the brokers incorrectly priced the index that day, when the Federal Reserve lowered short-term interest rates and sparked a sharp reaction in the municipal bond market. The six brokers named in the suit were Cantor, Fitzgerald Municipal Brokers Inc; Chapdelaine & Co; J.F. Hartfield & Co; J.J. Kenny Drake Inc; Municipal Partners Inc, and Titus & Donnelly Inc.

Vanguard alleges Thomson and the brokers, which Thomson's Bond Buyer unit uses to price its daily municipal bond index, committed breach of contract, negligent misrepresentation and violations of the Illinois consumer fraud and deceptive business practices act.

Vanguard said the Fed cut interest rates on December 19, 1995, at 1415 EST, and the price of both the Treasury bond and municipal bond index futures contracts other than the December muni contract rose dramatically.

But the Bond Buyer index "did not catch up with the bond market until the next day, December 20, 1995, when the rest of the bond market changed little from the previous day's close but the BBI rose 1-4/32," the suit said.
Thomson officials and the brokers named were not available for comment.
